title: Endophthalmitis After Cataract Surgery
description: Treat a painful hypopyon after cataract surgery as an emergency, sample and inject intravitreal antibiotics within the hour, choose vitrectomy by presenting vision, and prevent it with intracameral cefuroxime.
objectives: Recognize acute postoperative endophthalmitis and avoid a delaying trial of steroids
Sample the eye and give intravitreal vancomycin and ceftazidime at the correct doses
Use presenting vision to decide on immediate vitrectomy
Plan early review and supportive treatment

references.citation: Barry P, Cordovés L, Gardner S. ESCRS Guidelines for Prevention and Treatment of Endophthalmitis Following Cataract Surgery: Data, Dilemmas and Conclusions. Dublin: European Society of Cataract and Refractive Surgeons; 2013.

Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study Group. Results of the Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study. A randomized trial of immediate vitrectomy and of intravenous antibiotics for the treatment of postoperative bacterial endophthalmitis. Arch Ophthalmol. 1995;113(12):1479-1496.

Endophthalmitis Study Group, European Society of Cataract & Refractive Surgeons. Prophylaxis of postoperative endophthalmitis following cataract surgery: results of the ESCRS multicenter study and identification of risk factors. J Cataract Refract Surg. 2007;33(6):978-988.

start.text: A 72-year-old man is 5 days after uncomplicated cataract surgery on his right eye. Since yesterday the eye has become painful, red, and blurred. Vision is hand movements. There is a 2 mm hypopyon, and the fundus view is hazy.

diagnosis.text: What is your working diagnosis and plan?

options.label: Postoperative inflammation: intensify steroid drops and review in 48 hours
options.feedback: ESCRS 2013: presumed endophthalmitis is a medical emergency, because bacteria multiply exponentially and destroy visual potential. Do not delay diagnosis with a trial of steroid drops unless a sterile cause (toxic anterior segment syndrome) is strongly suspected.

options.label: Presumed acute postoperative endophthalmitis: sample the eye and inject antibiotics within the hour
options.feedback: ESCRS 2013: presumed endophthalmitis is a medical emergency needing investigation and treatment within an hour of presentation. Take an intraocular sample and give empirical intravitreal antibiotics. Blurred vision (93–94%), pain (74–79%), and hypopyon (72–85%) were the commonest presenting features in the EVS and ESCRS series.

hand_motion.text: His best vision is hand movements, and no vitreoretinal theatre is free for several hours. What now?

options.label: Vitreous biopsy with intravitreal vancomycin 1 mg and ceftazidime 2 mg, in separate syringes, now
options.feedback: EVS: with vision of hand movements or better, immediate vitrectomy gave no better outcome than a vitreous tap or biopsy. ESCRS 2013: when a vitrectomy theatre is not available promptly, vitreous biopsy with intravitreal antibiotics avoids delay. First-choice doses are vancomycin 1 mg plus ceftazidime 2 mg, in separate syringes and needles to prevent precipitation.

options.label: IV ceftazidime and amikacin, with intravitreal injection tomorrow
options.feedback: EVS: systemic ceftazidime and amikacin made no difference to final vision or media clarity. The intravitreal injection should not wait: ESCRS 2013 asks for sampling and intravitreal antibiotics within an hour of presentation.

options.label: Fortified topical antibiotics alone
options.feedback: ESCRS 2013: treatment of acute endophthalmitis is an intraocular sample with intravitreal antibiotics, given as an emergency. Topical antibiotics are at most an adjunct once intravitreal antibiotics have been given.

light_perception.text: His vision is light perception only. What now?

options.label: Vitreous tap and intravitreal antibiotics, avoiding theatre
options.feedback: EVS: with light perception only, immediate vitrectomy tripled the chance of reaching 20/40 (33% vs 11%) and halved severe visual loss (20% vs 47%) compared with a tap.

options.label: Immediate pars plana vitrectomy with intravitreal antibiotics
options.feedback: EVS: for light-perception-only vision, immediate vitrectomy increased the chance of 20/40 or better threefold (33% vs 11%) and halved severe visual loss (20% vs 47%). ESCRS 2013: inject intravitreal vancomycin 1 mg and ceftazidime 2 mg slowly at the end, considering a 50% dose reduction after a full vitrectomy.

aftercare.text: Which belong in his care over the next 2 days?

options.label: Clinical review about 6 hours after a tap and injection (12 hours after vitrectomy)
Topical steroid and atropine to prevent posterior synechiae
Chase the culture and sensitivity results
Repeat intravitreal antibiotics every 24 hours for 5 days
Intravitreal gentamicin 400 µg for Gram-negative cover

aftercare.feedback: ESCRS 2013: review 6 hours after a tap and injection, or 12 hours after vitrectomy; patients often worsen before improving. Start topical steroids and atropine, and chase microbiology results. Repeat intravitreal antibiotics only if needed, at 48–72-hour intervals; most eyes need one injection (7% of EVS patients were re-injected), and repeat injections increase retinal toxicity. Aminoglycoside doses have a narrow margin: gentamicin 400 µg may cause macular infarction.

prevention.text: At the unit's audit meeting you are asked how to prevent further cases. What do you recommend?

options.label: Postoperative topical antibiotic drops alone
options.feedback: In the ESCRS study, the absence of intracameral cefuroxime was associated with a 4.92-fold higher endophthalmitis risk. ESCRS 2013 notes that Swedish register data showed topical antibiotic drops added no clear benefit over the intracameral injection.

options.label: Intracameral cefuroxime 1 mg in 0.1 mL at the end of surgery, unless the patient is allergic to cephalosporins
options.feedback: ESCRS study: omitting intracameral cefuroxime 1 mg in 0.1 mL was associated with a 4.92-fold increase in endophthalmitis. Clear corneal incisions, silicone lenses, and surgical complications also raised risk. ESCRS 2013: cefuroxime's side chain differs from penicillins, so cross-reactivity is very low; Swedish practice withholds it only for cephalosporin allergy.

fail_delay.text: Complication: Delayed intravitreal treatment and vision loss.

fail_vitrectomy.text: Complication: Worse visual outcome without vitrectomy at light perception.

fail_aftercare.text: Complication: Retinal toxicity or synechiae from unsafe aftercare.

fail_prevention.text: Guideline Deviation: Prophylaxis without intracameral antibiotic.

success.text: Case Complete: Endophthalmitis treated and prevention improved.
